snschloss.name: Schwerin Castle
snschloss.slogan: A fairytale palace afloat on its own lake island.
snschloss.line: Rebuilt between 1845 and 1857, it is now part of the UNESCO-listed Schwerin Residence Ensemble.

snludwigslustschloss.name: Ludwigslust Palace
snludwigslustschloss.slogan: Sandstone gods on the roof, a ducal park below.
snludwigslustschloss.line: Its Golden Hall is decorated with Ludwigsluster Carton, a papier-mache that imitates stone and stucco.

snwismarmarkt.name: Wismar Market Square
snwismarmarkt.slogan: A vast Hanseatic square with a fountain from Holland.
snwismarmarkt.line: The Wasserkunst fountain was imported from Holland in 1602 and stands at the heart of one of northern Germany's largest squares.

sndom.name: Schwerin Cathedral
sndom.slogan: A brick spire that watches over the whole lake district.
sndom.line: Its 117.5-metre tower, finished in 1893, is the tallest church spire in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.

snwismarnikolai.name: St. Nikolai, Wismar
snwismarnikolai.slogan: The sailors' church, with a nave built to dwarf the harbour.
snwismarnikolai.line: Built between 1381 and 1460, it is known for the very lofty vaulting of its brick Gothic nave.
